title: It's 2021...Let's Talk About the Post-Apocalypse!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mtqdsr2BC_A

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens with the full Road Warrior monologue and a declaration of faith — Mad Max is the truth, The Road Warrior the legend, Beyond Thunderdome the myth, Fury Road one of the greatest films ever made — then walks his shelf of post-apocalyptic adventure games one box at a time.

Dark Venture is the closest thing to a Gamma World board game, the biggest game in the smallest box, inventive, flawed and sadly out of print. Fallen Land is the sprawling narrative option: hundreds of non-combat encounters, a burnt-out America, and an awful lot of bookkeeping. Defenders of the Last Stand is the traditional threat-management pick, Pandemic's five fires and three buckets in a wasteland coat. Post Human is a neat card-heavy trek that loses something solo. Waste Knights gets a nod as the pleasantly manageable newcomer. Shadows of Brimstone's Blasted Wastes earns high praise for its cargo-cult barter town. Aftermath is the one true story campaign — a charming critter crawl with a poor rulebook. Fallout he now calls a great game with the Atomic Bonds co-op expansion. Zona closes the tour for Stalker and Roadside Picnic readers.

A recurring thread: most of these play better competitively.

----

Daniel notes that post-apocalyptic games tend to work better competitively — is pitting survivor against survivor baked into the genre, or have designers just not cracked the co-op wasteland yet?
